topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: How Bouncing Blocks Calculate Digits of Pi

sections.title: Introduction: The Impossible Counting Puzzle
lecture_lines: Imagine two blocks colliding on a frictionless track.
A small block hits a massive one.
The collision count reveals digits of Pi.
How can simple physics calculate Pi?
animations: Fade in 'Block A' and 'Block B' on a horizontal line (white, #FFFFFF).
Animate the collision with a brief flash (red, #FF0000).
Display the number '3' appearing as a result of collision (yellow, #FFFF00).
Fade in the text 'Pi = 3.14...' below the blocks (white, #FFFFFF).

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
animations: Display P_1 and P_2 text objects (white, #FFFFFF).
Display KE_1 and KE_2 text objects (cyan, #00FFFF).
Animate arrows connecting momentum and energy to velocity labels (yellow, #FFFF00).

sections.title: The Geometry of Phase Space
lecture_lines: Plot block positions as XY coordinates.
Every collision is a boundary bounce.
animations: Draw a point moving along an angle (green, #00FF00).
Trace the path using a solid line (white, #FFFFFF).

sections.title: The Emergence of Pi
lecture_lines: Collision boundaries form a circular arc.
animations: Flash the Pi symbol to emphasize the connection (yellow, #FFFF00).

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Mechanical collisions act as analog computers.
